hints: Remember decomposition is the reverse reaction, so start reading the diagram from the right hand side at $2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$, not from the left.
The catalysed route is the lower curve with two humps, so moving leftwards from $2\text{NH}_3$ you first meet the small right-hand peak.
Activation energy is always measured upwards from the starting energy level to the top of that immediate peak for the step you are in.
walkthrough:
**Decide which direction is decomposition**

The forward reaction is $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$ left to right. Decomposition of $\text{NH}_3$ is the reverse, so we start at $2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$ on the right and move leftwards.

$$\text{starting level} = 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$$

**Pick out the catalysed pathway**

The uncatalysed route is the high single hump. The catalysed route is the lower curve with two humps, which means two steps with an intermediate in the middle.

$$\text{catalysed route} = \text{lower, two-peaked curve}$$

**Find the first step of the reverse catalysed route**

Moving left from $2\text{NH}_3$, the first barrier you meet is the small right-hand hump of the catalysed curve. Activation energy is the gap from the $2\text{NH}_3$ energy level up to the top of that hump, which is labelled D.

**Check the other arrows**

A is the tall uncatalysed forward barrier from $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$. B is the catalysed forward first step. C is the tall uncatalysed reverse barrier. Only D fits reverse, catalysed, first step.

options.A: A is the activation energy for the forward uncatalysed reaction. It goes from $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$ up to the top of the high single hump, not the reverse catalysed route.
options.B: B is the activation energy for the first step of the forward catalysed reaction. It starts from $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$ on the left, so it is the wrong direction for $\text{NH}_3$ decomposition.
options.C: C is the activation energy for the reverse uncatalysed reaction. It goes from $2\text{NH}_3$ up to the top of the high single hump, so it ignores the catalyst.
options.D: D is correct. Starting at $2\text{NH}_3$ and moving left along the lower catalysed curve, the first barrier is the right-hand small hump. D measures from the $2\text{NH}_3$ level to that peak, which is exactly the activation energy for the first step of catalysed decomposition.
